title: Linear form in $\log 2, \log 3, \log c$: explicit Baker–Wüstholz lower bound
author: @alon yuval
source: Implied by Matveev, Izv. Math. 64 (2000) 1217-1269 (restated as Bugeaud-Mignotte-Siksek, Ann. Math. 163 (2006), Thm 9.4). Verified against two independent open-access restatements that agree verbatim: arXiv:1905.01015 Thm 2.3 and arXiv:2207.12860 (Ddamulira-Luca) Thm 2.2: for positive real γ_i in a real field of degree D, Γ = ∏γ_i^{b_i} - 1 ≠ 0 ⇒ log|Γ| > -1.4·30^{t+3}·t^{4.5}·D²(1+log D)(1+log B)A_1⋯A_t, A_i ≥ max(D h(γ_i), |log γ_i|, 0.16). Here t=3, D=1, γ=(2,3,c), b=(k-1,-i,1), B ≤ 2i+1, A=(log 2, log 3, max(log c,0.16) ≤ log 4i): constant ≈ 9.9e10 vs 2^42 ≈ 4.4e12, margin ≈ 43x (checked for i=2^60..2^200); passing from Γ to Λ = log(Γ+1) costs at most log 2. Also implied by Baker-Wüstholz, J. reine angew. Math. 442 (1993) 19-62 (constant 2^42 as in rwst/bbchallenge, CC0).
